title: Distinguish proposed entities from existing implementation
statement: As an Architect or Developer, I can distinguish explicitly proposed technical entities from existing implementation and separately identify what is new relative to a comparison baseline so people and AI know both what remains to build and what a change introduced.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A proposed System, Component, or data entity can be recorded and referenced in a design before it has code evidence.
Entity documentation, deck references, and CLI queries expose proposed or implemented status explicitly; new is a separate comparison-relative classification, not a synonym for proposed.
An entity known to exist but lacking linked evidence is distinguishable from proposed work; missing, stale, or unresolved evidence remains visible and does not prove implementation.
Later addition of code evidence preserves the prior proposed definition and does not silently rewrite the committed plan.
A result classified as new identifies the comparison baseline and selected head; an entity can be both implemented and new in that comparison, and no baseline-free query silently invents newness.

An explicit operation can mark a proposed entity implemented while supplying scoped code references supporting that implementation; the operation refuses missing or unresolvable supplied evidence and preserves the prior proposal.

After implementation is recorded, proposed-work queries no longer classify that entity as proposed, while the same comparison can still identify it as new; unresolved or conflicting states remain visible.
Recording implemented status and code evidence does not itself record verification, integration, or review approval, and code currency remains a separately reported fact.
